I have a database of defects on plastic films. Defects are burns, holes, and similar things. Some defects are direction specific. A vertical sign on the material represents a scratch done on the material during the extrusion process. Data augmentation is a useful tool, but can be harmful for these defects. I was thinking about the possibility of implement a custom data augmentation related to the label of the training set. For example: a hole can be rotated without problems, but a scratch not. So I tell to the preprocessing layers how to do the augmentation by passing also the labels. Class 2 circuits are rendered safe by limiting the power supply to 100VA for circuits that operate at 30V or less, and the current to 5mA for circuits over 30V [Chapter 9, Table 11(A)] (**Fig. 1**). The power source for a Class 2 or a Class 3 circuit must be [725.121(A)]:. (2) A listed Class 2 or Class 3 power supply. (3) Equipment listed as a Class 2 or Class 3 power source. Class 2 and Class 3 circuits can be reclassified as a Class 1 circuit if the Class 2 and Class 3 equipment markings required by Sec. 725.124 are eliminated and the entire circuit is installed using a Chapter 3 wiring method per Part II of Art. 725 for Class 1 circuits.

See Sec. 725.41 for the voltage and power limitations of Class 1 circuits. To limit the spread of fire or products of combustion, the installation of Class 1 and Class 2 circuits must comply with Sec. 300.21 [Sec. 725.3(B)]. Class 1 and Class 2 circuits installed in ducts or plenums must comply with Sec. 300.22. Class 1, 2, and 3 circuits in cable trays must be installed per Parts I and II of Art. 392 [Sec. 725.3(E)]. Class 1 power-limited circuits must be supplied from a power supply that limits the output to 30V and no more than 1,000VA [Sec. 725.41(A)]. Class 1 remote-control and signaling circuits must not exceed 600V; the power output of the source need not be power limited Sec. 725.41(B)], as shown in **Fig. 2**. Class 1 circuit conductors supplied by a transformer having only a 2-wire secondary can be protected by the primary OCPD per Sec. 450.3(B), but only if the primary OCPD does not exceed the value determined by multiplying the secondary conductor ampacity by the secondary-to-primary transformer voltage ratio [Sec. 725.45(D)]. Class 1 circuits must be installed per Part I of Art. 300, and Class 1 wiring must be installed in a suitable Chapter 3 wiring method [Sec. 725.46]. Two or more Class 1 circuits can be installed in the same cable, enclosure, or raceway if all conductors are insulated for the maximum voltage of any conductor [Sec. 725.48(A)]. Class 1 circuits can be installed with electrical power conductors under any of the circumstances described in Sec. 725.48(B)(1) through (4). Class 1 circuit conductors must have at least a 600V insulation rating [Sec. 725.49(B)].

For validation I need sample points based on the area proportion (higher the area, more the points for that class). I converted raster to polygon and tried sampling using `Random Points inside polygon` but it does not create what I intend to get. What I need is random samples proportion to its size? PyQGIS solution would also work. This answer does the similar preprocessing but I want samples proportion to area of each class. Aman Bagrecha's user avatar. If you want [the number of] "...samples proportion to area of each class" you are referring to *density*, such as "one sample per hectare.". Next, determine what sampling density you wish to use. For example, let's say that your data is stored as meters and you wish your sampling density to be 1 point per hectare. **Pro tip:** Since there are 10,000 square meters in a hectare, an equivalent way to state our desired density is that we want 0.0001 points per square meter. Select your input polygon layer, where random points will be proportionally allocated according to feature size: larger polygons will receive more points (in our case at a rate of 1 point per hectare). Set the tool's *Sampling strategy* to Point density. Set the tool's *Point count or density* to 0.0001 (our **Pro tip** number). The documentation isn't clear, but *Point count or density* is expecting the number of desired samples *per CRS unit*, in our case square meters. - random points based on polygon size!
